headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data leakage from CrewAI’s shared workspace and broad egress into a non-runnable, offline course artifact; no direct pairwise execution path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory in a multi-agent crew, so attacker-controlled content in files can be treated as instructions. The zoomcamp profile is a non-runnable course artifact with no runtime defenses, so the pairwise bridge is indirect but plausible. No direct documented interaction exists, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF CrewAI ingests files from the shared working directory as prompts or tool instructions, injection is possible.
IF the course materials are copied into CrewAI-managed files, malicious text can influence downstream agent behavior.
mitigations: Separate prompt files from untrusted course materials in different directories.
Add a manual review step before CrewAI reads any imported text.
Disable automatic file ingestion for any content sourced from the zoomcamp repo.
Use a read-only mount for course materials.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all file-fed prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and it has broad network egress plus filesystem access. The zoomcamp artifact itself is offline, but if its materials are placed into CrewAI’s workspace, sensitive developer inputs could be exposed through logs, outputs, or model-provider calls. The pairwise leakage path is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive crew inputs are stored in the same workspace as zoomcamp materials, CrewAI may read them.
IF CrewAI sends workspace content to model providers, copied course files can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Run CrewAI with a dedicated empty working directory.
Redact API keys before any file-based processing.
Restrict outbound network destinations where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and content filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write access to the host working directory, while the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and exposes no write surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is only if the course repo is manually copied into CrewAI’s workspace. Uncertainty is limited because B lacks mutable runtime capabilities.
conditions: IF the zoomcamp materials are mounted into the same writable directory as CrewAI, file clobbering can occur.
IF an operator manually edits shared files while CrewAI runs, local conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount shared inputs read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Snapshot the workspace before running CrewAI.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around any shared mutable path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI’s role-playing crew and shared memory can propagate one agent’s output to another without strong verification. The zoomcamp artifact is a course repo, so if its content is used as reference material, CrewAI may treat it as authoritative and amplify mistakes into generated actions or summaries. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF CrewAI uses zoomcamp text as source material, downstream agents may repeat its errors.
IF CrewAI agents act on unverified extracted facts, mistakes can cascade into outputs.
mitigations: Require citation checks before any action-taking step.
Insert a verification agent between extraction and execution.
Mark course content as untrusted input.
Limit CrewAI to summarization only.
requires-engineering: add structured validation for all inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while the zoomcamp profile is a public open-source course with no sensitive data class or residency constraints. No PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch is evidenced here, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling hygiene. The other agent is not cited beyond its public, non-sensitive nature.
conditions: IF sensitive developer data is placed into CrewAI alongside public course materials, retention and logging policies must be reviewed.
IF the operator uses CrewAI for regulated data, separate compliance controls are required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pairing.
Review logging settings before execution.
Store secrets in a dedicated secret manager.
Use a public-data-only workspace.
requires-engineering: implement data-class-based retention controls.
